title: fix(sessions): reuse committed row facts during refresh
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-list refreshes reread entry, participant, and summary-watermark facts that the Gateway already received from the same committed write.

## User Impact

Session rows reuse committed facts during transcript updates and entry snapshot enrichment, reducing repeated worker reads without changing stored data, permissions, schema, or update behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The entry publisher compared a process-wide transcript notification counter before exposing a receipt. Installing a combined entry/transcript receipt advances that counter itself, so the publisher could discard its own current watermark. The row projection separately correlated display notifications with another retained transcript-authority object. Message-less or delayed notifications therefore discarded usable facts.

Use the existing receipt owner: remove both global-counter comparisons and the duplicate notification authority, and retain the actor's Board/summary projection when entry reads add snapshot fields. Starting a new actor command also keeps the previous committed snapshot until a write changes its token; a stale reader evicts that snapshot without canceling the pending command's fresh receipt. Entry, participant display, and watermark facts remain covered by the same committed-write token. Physical source binding, keyed receipt supersession, membership revocation, and current authority at real effects remain enforced. No new cache, SQL, fencing, or worker handshake is introduced.

Removed checks and accepted edges:

- Process-wide transcript-counter capture/rechecks: an unrelated session notification no longer discards this row's receipt. Gateway writes remain ordered through receipt installation; unsupported reentrant native writes from a delivery callback may briefly retain earlier display facts until the writer publishes.
- Notification session/lifecycle/message/sequence correlation and duplicate `Row.transcriptAuthority`: a delayed or message-less notification may schedule an unnecessary refresh of the current row. Notifications never supply the stored watermark.
- Eager replica eviction at command start: readers may observe the preceding committed snapshot while the next command awaits execution, just as a database snapshot read would. The existing write token rejects it after commit; effectful commands still validate current worker-owned state. Stale-read eviction no longer revokes the pending receipt.

Writer coverage remains with existing receipts/tokens: entry create/update/snapshots, aliases/reset/delete; owner/member/participant changes including count-only participant writes; Board changes; native session deletion; append/bulk/rewrite/import/suffix/compaction; cold archive/restore and projection rebuild; window/cascade deletion; raw fixture clears. Scoped writes invalidate the affected key/session; unscoped DML advances the token shared by every scope. Unknown outcomes revoke facts. The change preserves only previously current projection facts; it does not carry an old watermark across a new metadata-write token.

Related: #169748. Reuses the projection-watermark idiom from #169753 without changing its reply-tail implementation.

## Evidence

### Landing integration

Current head `8b6a8830f16b67fad3bb0cb5cc06f964d4c7b0cf` merges main `acc5395d48360aedc1dd7353085e1d9d315b3efc` without conflicts or optimization changes. [Current-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38260588359) tests merge `6535906e035a7fbb118c28f38683a7de616aaf7c` against main `157216b8e37486575e3217b297a49bcb12ffad6f`. The run completed with 50 successful jobs, 24 skipped, and no failures, including its aggregate CI gate. Production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts/export collisions, architecture/Madge, and T1/dialect ratchets passed. All three changed test files were included in the successful PR shard jobs: the preflight lists them, and changed runnable tests are mandatory in both aggressive selection and runtime filtering (including the PR-exempt accepted-facts test). No per-file integrated-run counts or timings are claimed. Earlier live measurements and review evidence below are retained as measured-head evidence, not relabeled as a new live run.

The current-head [Knip production scan](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38260690195/job/114850526910) reports only unused exported type `src/infra/directory-durability.ts: DurableDirectoryReceipt`, identically reported by [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38258960208/job/114844763380) at `12d02f7a3eae579ab151b3c4c44e08a31bbd2f76`. The offending file is byte-identical on the integrated base and head and is untouched by this PR. This inherited failure is recorded in the red-main repair inbox. The production scan covers all six changed production files and reports no lane findings. Its failure prevents the chained full-tree/unused-file/script scans, which are not claimed green; this lane changes no script/config/SDK export surface, adds/removes no files, and its three changed tests export nothing. The remaining optional manual workflow was canceled and confirmed stopped after preserving this result.

### Measured-head evidence

**Measured head `d006ccf0a7b47496b15f96f0c7444cfa31ff74c2`: all changed tests, required static checks, both Codex review rounds, and the final isolated Gateway workload passed.** Production is byte-identical to build head `0f0de4ce48c7ad4656778847909bd3fcefbc1a67`; all 19 recorded source hashes matched after the run. The full `qaRuntime` build passed in 2095.8 seconds. ClawSweeper's final-head review reported no findings.

One baseline/final-candidate comparison uses the shared harness's same ten warmed turns, pinned baseline `242ef62b2645e24416f5d654c9af1176aec242f9` and final head above. Counts include all Gateway threads and background work. The final run passed all 13 turns, control RPCs, child run, cron, compaction, and graceful shutdown in 190.2 seconds. Baseline completed all turns and lifecycle but its final all-RPC assertion failed because `mentions.dismiss` returned `UNAVAILABLE`; its warmed measurements reconcile with native counters. No unloaded-host timing claim is made.

The targeted `session-row-facts` operation drops from 26 to 5.5 SQL statements/turn: **20.5 fewer statements and 4.1 fewer requests per warmed turn**. Row-fact calls are one in nine warmed turns and two in one turn; the strict ≤1 target is therefore narrowly missed. Watermark reads include one remaining patch-commit predicate per turn, so its ≤1 total target is not reached. `sessionRows.sharedFacts` additionally falls by 2.4 statements and 3.9 requests/turn. Whole-turn mean savings are 34.4 statements and 12.5 requests; these include scheduling-dependent background differences, not solely this owner change.

All row-fact calls originate from `src/gateway/session-row-projection-refresh.ts:refreshBatch` → `readRows` → `session-row-database-facts.ts:withSessionRowDatabaseFacts`, consuming the entry/participants/summary-watermark triple. Each costs five statements including its consistent-read transaction. Watermark reads are these row-fact reads plus `session-entry-patch-guard.ts:readSessionEntryPatchPredicate`. Remaining projection reads are hydration (2/turn), row backfill (1.8), anchor lookup (1), patch predicate (1), and activity-summary source (1); no request duplicates its projection read. Reuse across these requests requires cold/reset/index facts not carried by current receipts, so those consistent snapshots remain.

Actor hydration rises by six SELECTs across the ten warmed turns (6.0 → 6.6/turn). Standalone `session.actor.read` requests/hydrations rise 40 → 44. With command counts unchanged, `deliverySettled` hydrations rise 6 → 9 and `adoptRun` 0 → 1, while `appendTranscriptEvent` falls 14 → 12. The complete +0.6 is retained in the net savings above; it is not dismissed as noise.

Every standalone hydration in both runs follows canonical native mutation statements since the preceding actor completion. Final delivery hydrations generally follow `completeTurn` → usage release → entry patch; the adoption hydration follows a memory-cache write. `src/config/sessions/session-actor.worker.ts:read` rehydrates when the resident's scoped write token differs. `src/infra/sqlite-database-write-receipts.ts:scopedWriteToken` includes the unscoped revision, so usage/memory writes can invalidate the resident; `session-actor.worker.ts:prepareEntryPatch` cannot preserve an already stale resident. These owners and `src/config/sessions/session-actor-sqlite.ts:read` are unchanged by this PR. However, removing awaited reads can change execution order, and the trace records executed mutations rather than affected-row counts or token values. This establishes a plausible mechanism, not independence from this change.

Known tradeoff: actor hydration +0.6 reads/turn, owned by the exactentry lane's actor-hydration investigation.

The coordinator explicitly approved landing with this disclosed cost on 2026-10-12; it is included in the measured net reduction above.

The final fixture required a documented startup adaptation. Two attempts timed out during first-time pairing at the unchanged 15-second handshake deadline, before any turn. A task-local harness copy now calls the existing `requestDevicePairing` and `approveDevicePairing` APIs before Gateway startup, closes that isolated state owner, and then uses the original nonce/signature/role/scope handshake. The shared harness, production code, runtime deadlines, and measured workload are unchanged. The first pre-paired attempt exceeded the unchanged 300-second readiness deadline under heavy host load; waiting for load ≤80 and entering the canonical five-slot gate produced a successful run (Gateway ready in 63.64 seconds).

Pre-pair setup is separately instrumented and included in the raw whole-workload totals: 1,637 SQL statements and 2,324 sends, of which 2,320 are the TypeScript loader's compiler traffic and four are owner open/request/approve/close operations. This explains the raw whole-request increase; none occurs in a warmed turn. Pre-initializing shared state also moves startup work out of Gateway MAIN, so its whole-workload decrease is not claimed as a production improvement. The warmed MAIN count is unchanged; its two statements across ten turns are unrelated GitHub OAuth maintenance. All fixture processes exited, the harness directory was removed, and the proof slot was released.

T1: changed row-fact/receipt owners **0 → 0**. Shared transcript readers retain **8 → 8** flagged call sites: active-context 6, projection-read 1, watermark wrapper 1. These still serve released synchronous `SessionManager` APIs, process-held incognito paths, the CLI history effect guard, and the legacy SDK reply-start adapter. Moving those calls requires their API/owner cutover; they remain explicitly flagged under the requested escape hatch, not reclassified as worker-only. Baseline global inventory: 537 T1 calls in 200 files.

Regression coverage extends existing tests for combined entry+transcript receipts, unrelated/message-less notifications, and actor snapshot enrichment followed by an in-process append. Existing tests retain native owner/replacement/delete, participant count-only, raw write, rollback, archive, and membership-revocation coverage. The old synthetic callback-interleaving matrix was removed with its duplicate check.

Basic scoped oxfmt/oxlint and `git diff --check` passed. Both Codex autoreview rounds completed clean, with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final two-line test-fixture correction keeps `updated_at` and `entry_json.updatedAt` consistent in the native transaction; it changes no production code and passed the final actor test run.

Measured-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38246099756) passed all production/test type stripes, lint, source contracts/export collisions, Madge, T1/dialect ratchets, guards, boundaries, docs, and build. It tested merge `6f20a979` into main `8f164a15f2d6ffaf06ba48e6932a5dc3f8b7768f`. Exact-head [Knip](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38246203641/job/114800939590) passed all three export scans with zero entries (about 158 seconds). The manual CI job containing it stopped in an earlier, unrelated `server.agent-artifact-apis.test.ts:515` config during agent deletion/resource drainage; its stop-on-failure setting never invoked the accepted-facts config. This is an observed optional-manual failure, not a claimed matching main failure. The focused run's unusually long wall time includes 535.026 seconds of cold worker preparation and heavy-host module transforms; it is not the cost of the added assertions alone. No broad local suite or remote lease was used. There is no SDK surface change or update/Doctor/migration/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle change, so no SDK diff or published-driver update cell is required.

The earlier measured-head aggregate PR gate was red for seven Bun installer HTTP 504 failures before test execution and one inherited assertion: [`session-utils.metadata-perf.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38246099756/job/114800840035), “rebuilds resident thinking facts on config and catalog publication,” expects `high` and receives `medium` at line 168. [Scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38243573908/job/114792154319), SHA `70885c1bbbdaa930ab085d28af40c55dde87fffa`, fails the same assertion. It is recorded in the campaign's red-main repair inbox. This PR does not modify that file.

The earlier measured-head [Security High / network-ssrf-boundary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38246099168/job/114800232736) also stopped before analysis because both CodeQL CLI download paths returned HTTP 504. It produced no security finding. `security-fast`, all other Security High categories, and [`openclaw/security-sensitive-review`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38247450104) passed. The documented infrastructure/inherited failures qualify for the authorized relaxed landing policy; the failed jobs are not represented as green. The coordinator approved the disclosed hydration tradeoff described above; the final live workload passed.

## Receipt and invalidation contract

`src/infra/sqlite-database-admission.ts:beginSqliteDatabaseWrite` and `finishSqliteDatabaseWrite` settle the shared in-process write receipt. Scoped writes advance the affected logical-key/session-ID tokens; unclassified writes invalidate all scopes. Failed or rolled-back writes may conservatively invalidate facts. `S/session-actor-replica.ts` compares `readSqliteDatabaseScopedWriteTokenForPath` for the logical key and dependent physical session IDs before reusing retained facts. This is an in-memory receipt lookup, not a SQLite freshness query.

The direct infrastructure regression is `src/infra/sqlite-database-admission.worker.test.ts` — **"shares exact session receipts with existing writer isolates and fences unclassified writes"**. It checks targeted invalidation, dependency registration visible to an existing worker, and unclassified raw-write invalidation of both cached scopes.

Complete row facts must come from one database snapshot or one complete accepted receipt. A partial entry, owner, membership, participant, or transcript publication does not certify that the other members of the triple are unchanged. A transcript-content receipt marked unchanged also does not certify unchanged hot/cold/index state.
